core_obligations: Set up the uniform reduction: for a property P stable under base change and composition and holding for closed immersions, reduce 'P + universally injective implies radicial' to the statement that a nonempty reduced algebraic space X over a field K, with X -> Spec(K) universally injective and having P, is representable by the spectrum of a field (proof lines 113-132).

Case (1): check the hypothesis of that reduction for P = decent via the three Decent Spaces lemmas, then use that |X| is a singleton together with the decent criterion to get X = Spec(L) for an extension K subset L (proof lines 135-147).
Case (2): a quasi-separated morphism is decent, so (1) implies (2) (proof lines 150-153).

Case (3): for locally separated f choose a surjective etale U -> X with U affine, show that j : U x_X U -> U x_{Spec(K)} U is both surjective (universally injective) and an immersion (locally separated), hence a closed immersion, so that R = U x_X U is affine and X = U/R is quasi-separated, reducing to (2) (proof lines 156-184).
proof_roadmap: Prove the uniform reduction for a property P stable under base change and composition and containing closed immersions (proof lines 113-132).

Verify P = decent, quasi-separated, locally separated in turn and run the reduced statement, with the locally separated case using the surjective immersion j to reach the quasi-separated case (proof lines 135-184).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is about a universally injective morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over a scheme S and claims radiciality under each of three separation hypotheses, decent, quasi-separated, locally separated (statement lines 101-110). The proof first isolates a uniform implication 'P + universally injective => radicial' for any property P stable under base change and composition and holding for closed immersions, then discharges it in the field case using decentness, and finally runs the three cases (proof lines 113-184). The part that cannot be done by citing alone is the locally separated case: one must build the affine presentation U -> X and prove that j : U x_X U -> U x_{Spec(K)} U is at once surjective and an immersion, so that a surjective immersion is a closed immersion and R becomes affine (proof lines 171-184). That is a genuine geometric step, but it is standard and fully guided, so H2.
